Article Title: How Jadumani Singh's risky weight change nearly derailed his CWG dream before winning Glasgow silver
Article Text:
India's Jadumani Singh Mandengbam (PTI Photo)

A bold gamble after the 50kg category disappeared

The selection maze before Glasgow

Jadumani Si​ngh's Road to CWG Silver (AI-generated Infographic)

The Sports Ministry hurdle

Jadumani Singh Mandengbam (PTI Photo)

Why the gold slipped away

File Pic: L Sarita Devi (PTI Photo)

Olympic gold remains the ultimate dream

NEW DELHI: When Indian pugilist Jadumani Singh Mandengbam stepped onto the podium to receive the men's 55kg silver medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, it marked the culmination of a journey that had almost ended before it had even begun.The 22-year-old Manipuri boxer was one of India's standout performers, winning four consecutive unanimous 5-0 verdicts to storm into the bantamweight final before settling for silver against Australia's Jye Dixon. His medal also formed part of India's historic boxing campaign, which yielded seven golds and three silvers, making the country the No. 1 boxing nation at the Games for the first time.Yet, behind that success lay months of uncertainty, selection hurdles and a weight-category gamble that nearly cost him a place on the flight to Scotland.Speaking exclusively to TimesofIndia.com, former world champion and Jadumani's mentor, Laishram Sarita Devi, recounted how the young boxer refused to abandon his Olympic dream even when every obstacle seemed stacked against him.Jadumani had built his reputation in the 50kg category, winning medals at World Boxing Cups before learning that the division would no longer feature in the Commonwealth Games, Asian Games or Olympic programme.Rather than remain in a non-Olympic category, he decided to move up to 55kg — a division already occupied by some of India's biggest names."He continued to consult with me. Whenever he had to make a big decision, he called up and consulted with me — like increasing his weight category," Sarita told TimesofIndia.com."After he won a World Cup medal in 50kg, he got to know that the weight category is no longer in the CWG, Asian Games and Olympics. He wanted to move to 55kg."The decision immediately brought fresh challenges."Army had their No. 1 boxer in the 55kg category in Pune, who is Services' No. 1 boxer. And the weight category also has Amit Panghal — Olympian and Asian champion. He said he wanted to move up the weight to compete at CWG, Asian Games etc, but was discouraged by hearing questions like whether he would be able to compete at that level, which created a doubt in him," she said.Sarita, however, wanted only one answer: "We sat down and I asked him, 'Are you confident about the decision?' He said he was, so I told him to move up the category."The decision created another problem.Without competing in the National Championships, Jadumani could not enter the national coaching camp. But because he belonged to the Army Sports Institute, Services already had its designated 55kg representative. Attempts to let him represent Manipur also failed."We tried to make him compete for the state of Manipur, but we didn't get an NOC because he is with the Army," Sarita said.Relief finally arrived through a Boxing Federation of India (BFI) policy that granted direct entries to the National Championships for World Boxing Cup medallists. The move was aimed at rewarding elite international performers and ensuring they were not blocked by the usual domestic qualification pathways.The decision allowed Jadumani to compete directly in the 55kg draw despite the institutional overlap, resulting in multiple squad members — Pawan Bartwal, Jadumani Singh and Amit Panghal — finding themselves in the same weight-category draw.Sarita said her ward grabbed the opportunity with both hands."He then got a chance to compete in 55kg in the Nationals. Due to his effort, he won against the Services No.1, Olympians etc to be named Best Boxer in the Nationals. After that he got the chance to be part of the India camp," she said.He then cleared the final selection trials, which included physical assessments alongside ring performances."He participated in the final trial for the CWG and Asian Games — which had many aspects like strength and endurance tests before fighting in the ring. He won all of it to get selected for the CWG and was really happy and started training hard," she added.Just when Glasgow appeared certain, another setback emerged.Because Jadumani had only recently moved into 55kg, he did not possess the Asian ranking required under the Sports Ministry's eligibility criteria for Commonwealth Games selection."He got an explanation mail from the Sports Ministry, which put him in immense tension ahead of the Games," Sarita recalled.Under the ministry's guidelines, boxers were expected to be ranked among Asia's top eight in their respective categories."He was ranked No. 2 in 50kg, but he lacked a ranking in the new 55kg category. He had only competed in one Asian Championship in the new weight category before the trials for CWG and, being new to the category, lost in the quarterfinals," she said.That led to fresh doubts over his selection."He was disheartened when questions were raised whether he was a medal prospect because he was not in the rankings prescribed by the ministry. He called me and said the coaches were saying he may or may not be on the flight to the CWG because of this letter from the ministry," she recalled.The uncertainty only ended after BFI submitted a detailed explanation to the ministry, outlining Jadumani's circumstances following his weight-category switch."BFI replied to the ministry properly, explaining everything and after a lot of effort his ticket to Glasgow was approved. What I like about him is that he is the kind of person who doesn't give up and has a very strong will power," she said.Jadumani eventually reached the final after four demanding contests, each won by an identical 5-0 margin. But Sarita believes the scheduling ultimately worked against him."Jadumani's four bouts were very tough. He played all out in all the bouts till the semifinals as he got proper rest and recovery time. Since the gold medal opponent got a bye earlier, he had fewer bouts than Jadumani," she explained.The semifinal-final turnaround, she felt, proved decisive. There was a one-day gap after every bout until the semifinals, but there was no gap between the semifinal and final in Glasgow."Jadumani fought his semifinal in the evening and got the final bout the next morning only, so he did not get much time for recovery. If it was in the evening, he could have fought better. When he entered the ring for the final, I saw his face and body language sitting here and realised he had not had enough recovery," she said.The experience, she believes, underlines the growing importance of sports science."In such situations, we should look for how we can enhance or speed up the recovery process through sports science. We should discuss it to make sure our boxers can give 100 per cent every time they enter the ring," she added.Sarita first noticed Jadumani as a youngster competing in a local tournament."When I saw Jadumani for the first time, it was a tournament for young boys. His movement was really pleasing and I thought he could become a good boxer in the future. I identified him at that time only and gave him Rs 500 because I was very pleased with his performance," she recalled."Jadumani did not start with me from the grassroots. He learnt his basics from another academy. He came to my academy when he was preparing to enrol in the Army Sports Institute in Pune. At that time, I did not have any infrastructure and was coaching from a makeshift setup. And then Covid happened, we had to train in a very isolated small makeshift place,” she added.Years later, after training together through difficult Covid-19 conditions and watching him overcome one hurdle after another, Sarita believes Glasgow is only the beginning."We missed gold at the CWG, but we will work hard to get gold at the Asian Games for sure," she said.The bigger ambition, however, stretches far beyond continental success."His first and primary target remains Olympic gold. Commonwealth Games and Asian Games are the stepping stones in that journey. He will try to win India's first Olympic gold medal in boxing," Sarita concluded.
Article Summary: Jadumani Singh Mandengbam won silver at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. The 22-year-old Manipuri boxer won four consecutive unanimous 5-0 verdicts to storm into the bantamweight final before settling for silver against Australia's Jye Dixon. His medal also formed part of India's historic boxing campaign, which yielded seven golds and three silvers, making the country the No. 1 boxing nation at the Games.

Article Title: 'Officials will contact': CM Pushkar Singh Dhami responds to Rishabh Pant's emotional land appeal
Article Text:
Uttarakhand's CM Pushkar Singh Dhami and Rishabh Pant (ANI Image)

Pant wants to return to his roots

'I want to buy it, not receive it as a gift'

CM Dhami assures cooperation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami has responded to India wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant 's public appeal for help in acquiring land in his home state, assuring the cricketer that the government will extend all possible assistance in accordance with the rules.Pant, who is currently in Sri Lanka with the Indian team ahead of the two-Test series, had taken to social media platform X in the early hours of Saturday to seek the chief minister's intervention after struggling to purchase land in Uttarakhand for nearly three years.In a heartfelt post, the 28-year-old revealed his desire to move his base from Delhi to Uttarakhand and build his first home in the state where his roots lie. Pant said that despite searching for suitable land for the past three years, he had been unable to find a property that met his requirements."@pushkardhami hello sir how’s you ??? It’s a long time for me especially being local from Uttrakhand . I have been trying to buy land to shift my base from Delhi to Uttrakhand and I couldn’t find anything facilitating and big to live here I love my Uttrakhand. My humble request to us is please help me in land acquisition cause nowadays it had become nitemare with clarity and even other land is dew which was I supposedly get when I was promoting the state before keeping everything in side I wanna move back to my native place to help and built around Uttrakhand and I want to shif back to my Pahadi people please look into this matter it’s been 3 years didn’t get any land awaiting your answer @pushkardhami sir," Pant wrote on X.Pant later clarified that he was not seeking any special favour or free allotment from the government. Instead, he said he was willing to purchase the land at the government's prescribed rates if the administration could facilitate the process."A gift would be lovey for representation out states at the highest level internationally stages but if you allow me I wanna buy it fromGovernment and on there rates at least I can have my first house built in my own state and our state please be helpful. Seriously didn’t know how to do it," he further wrote.Responding to Pant's appeal, Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami praised the India star for bringing laurels to Uttarakhand and welcomed his desire to return to his home state."Dear Rishabh, you are the pride of Uttarakhand. With your splendid performances and achievements, you have illuminated the name of Devbhoomi across the country and the world. Your love for your motherland and your desire to return and contribute here are truly commendable," Dhami posted on X.The chief minister further confirmed that the matter had been referred to the concerned authorities."Instructions are being issued to the concerned officials. They will contact you soon and ensure all possible cooperation in accordance with the rules," he added.
Article Summary: India wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant has made a public appeal for help in acquiring land in his home state Uttarakhand. Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami has responded to Pant's appeal, assuring the cricketer that the government will extend all possible assistance in accordance with the rules. Pant is currently in Sri Lanka with the Indian team ahead of the two-Test series.

Article Title: India vs Sri Lanka: Captain Shubman Gill's time to take centrestage
Article Text:
India's captain Shubman Gill, (left), and head coach Gautam Gambhir during a training session. (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

It's been a year since a young Indian team came out of a grueling five-Test tour of England with a memorable 2-2 scoreline. "Our next four Test matches are going to be in India. And that's going to be a different challenge. We have enough talent. This series was very important for us. Every player would feel a lot mature after the end of the series and that would really help us in the long run in this WTC cycle," Shubman Gill , otherwise measured with his words during the tour, found an assertive tone to his speech after the dramatic win in the fifth Test at The Oval.Well, the subsequent home season ended up derailing India's World Test Championship campaign with South Africa steamrolling India in the two Test matches in Nov. If the heroics in England was deemed as India's Test redemption for the preceding forgettable tour of Australia, the consolidation post the English summer never arrived. Instead, an undeniably edgy Indian team has now arrived in Sri Lanka for a two-Test series with the desperation of staying alive in the WTC.Gill became the face of India's Test cricket in England. But the mind was undoubtedly head coach Gautam Gambhir 's. Gill arrived in England understandably like deer in the headlights after being thrust to captaincy post the debacle in Australia which saw the retirements of three stalwarts in Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma and Ravichandran Ashwin.Gambhir was his shepherd in the chaos. "Before the start of the series, Gauti bhai (Gambhir) said we are a young team but we want to be looked at as a gun team," Gill had revealed Gambhir's nerve-settling words.Gambhir did the heavy-lifting to ensure Gill the batter didn't succumb to the pressures of leading an inexperienced team in England. One can't write off Gambhir's overbearing influence in Test and T20 teams in the last one year. Perhaps, it's time Gill came out of Gambhir's shadow to resurrect India's reputation as a Test team.When he steps out for the toss in Galle on Aug 15, it will be his 10th Test as India captain which includes a Test against South Africa where he was ruled out due to a neck injury after playing three balls in the game. He has led in 12 ODIs. Technically, his captaincy career is still in its nascent stage. But current circumstances won't allow him much time before the swords are pulled out.It's unusual for Indian cricket to have a captain playing the second fiddle in the engine room. Every Indian team is eventually remembered by the captain it had. TOI understands that the power forces in the BCCI have been encouraging Gill to have a firmer say in planning. If the last two ODI series are anything to go by, one may say that Gill has been taking the initiative to drive his point across with the senior players in the team. He was assertive in his demand for bigger windows for preparing for crucial Test series.The team management, with Gambhir facing the heat for India's Test performances, would want to retain Gill batting with as little pressure as possible. Post the series against South Africa, Gambhir himself alluded to the fact that missing the regular captain had a detrimental effect on the undercooked batting order. Yet, India would want Gill absolutely in charge when he is leading the team on the field.In the first eight Tests that he captained, it was apparent that he had very little say in the XI that took the field. Be it the inexplicable reluctance to bowl Shardul Thakur and Nitish Kumar Reddy in a Test match or under-bowling Washington Sundar, Gill is yet to blossom into the undisputed decision-maker in the dressing room. One surely wouldn't want a captain walking out with a team with the thought of using just 10 players.However, people close to the team management claim that he has come a long way from being the clueless captain fielding at long-off in the Manchester Test where KL Rahul literally took charge of marshalling the players in the field as Ben Stokes cruised to a century. Sources say he has opened communication channels with players, even reaching out to them after selection meetings and discussing their roles in the team.It is learnt Gill has become more vocal and assertive about his choices while leading Gujarat Titans, a franchise that swears by the tactical acumen of head coach Ashish Nehra.Save the England tour, the torrid Test record during Gambhir's tenure has left him very little breathing space. With India's chances in the WTC hanging by a thread, chief selector Ajit Agarkar too will have to face the heat if the results don't go their way. Yet, Gill has to quickly emerge as the one who is firmly in charge if this team has to discover its true identity.
Article Summary: Shubman Gill is yet to blossom into the undisputed decision-maker in the dressing room. The power forces in the BCCI have been encouraging Gill to have a firmer say in planning. The team management, with Gambhir facing the heat for India's Test performances, would want Gill batting with as little pressure as possible.

Article Title: Rishabh Pant's midnight plea to Uttarakhand CM: 'Please help me in land acquisition' as star seeks to build home in state
Article Text:
Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami; and Rishabh Pant (Agency Photos)

Pant wants to move back to his roots

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

From Rs 27 crore IPL deal to massive endorsements

NEW DELHI: India wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant made a rather unusual public appeal in the early hours of Saturday, directly requesting Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami to help him acquire land in the state so he can shift his base from Delhi and build his first home in his native state.Pant, who is currently in Sri Lanka with the Indian team for the two-match Test series, took to social media platform X to make the request, tagging Dhami in a lengthy post. The 28-year-old said he had been trying to find suitable land in Uttarakhand for the past three years but had struggled to find a property that could meet his requirements.More importantly, Pant made it clear that he wanted to return to his roots and contribute to the state after years of representing India on the international stage."@pushkardhami hello sir how’s you ??? It’s a long time for me especially being local from Uttrakhand . I have been trying to buy land to shift my base from Delhi to Uttrakhand and I couldn’t find anything facilitating and big to live here I love my Uttrakhand. My humble request to us is please help me in land acquisition cause nowadays it had become nitemare with clarity and even other land is dew which was I supposedly get when I was promoting the state before keeping everything in side I wanna move back to my native place to help and built around Uttrakhand and I want to shif back to my Pahadi people please look into this matter it’s been 3 years didn’t get any land awaiting your answer @pushkardhami sir," he wrote.Pant followed it up by clarifying that he was not asking for land as a free gift, but wanted to purchase it from the government at the applicable rates."A gift would be lovey for representation out states at the highest level internationally stages but if you allow me I wanna buy it fromGovernment and on there rates at least I can have my first house built in my own state and our state please be helpful. Seriously didn’t know how to do it," he further wrote.The posts quickly went viral, with Pant's unusual request drawing significant attention on social media.Pant was born in Roorkee in Uttarakhand's Haridwar district and began his cricketing journey there before moving to Delhi to pursue the sport professionally. He eventually established himself as one of India's premier wicketkeeper-batters across formats.Although Pant continues to represent Delhi in domestic cricket, he has repeatedly maintained a strong connection with Uttarakhand. His latest posts underline his desire to eventually make the state his home and contribute to its development.His appeal also comes just days after Pant emerged as Uttarakhand's highest individual taxpayer for the 2025-26 financial year, having reportedly paid Rs 23.84 crore in income tax.The figures were announced by the Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, Uttarakhand, during an event marking Income Tax Day on July 24. Pant topped the list of individual taxpayers in the state for the second consecutive year.According to figures reported by ABP Live, Pant's tax contribution more than doubled from the previous financial year, when he had paid around Rs 10.5 crore in advance tax.Pant's enormous tax outgo reflects his earnings from several sources, including his BCCI contract, IPL salary, match fees and endorsement deals.He was bought by Lucknow Super Giants for Rs 27 crore, making him one of the most expensive players in the league. During the assessed period, Pant was also a Grade A BCCI-contracted cricketer, earning an annual retainership of Rs 5 crore. He has since been moved to Grade B, with his annual retainership reduced to Rs 3 crore.His commercial earnings add significantly to his income. Pant has endorsement associations with Adidas, Dream11, SG, Thums Up, Cadbury, boAt, Noise, Zomato, JSW Cement and MakeMyTrip.
Article Summary: India wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant made a rather unusual public appeal in the early hours of Saturday. Pant asked Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami to help him acquire land in the state. The 28-year-old said he had been trying to find suitable land for the past three years but had struggled to find a property that could meet his requirements.

Article Title: IRE vs AFG 2nd ODI: Rashid Khan's six-for helps Afghanistan crush Ireland by 92 runs
Article Text:
Rashid Khan in action during the second ODI against Ireland. (Pic credit: Afghanistan Cricket)

Ibrahim, Atal lay foundation for Afghanistan

Rashid sparks Ireland collapse

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Brief Scores: Afghanistan 299/8 in 47 overs (Ibrahim Zadran 84, Sediqullah Atal 45; Mark Adair 2-40, Jay Moondra 2-78) beat Ireland 207 all-out in 33.4 overs (Cade Carmichael 62, Andy Balbirnie 36; Rashid Khan 6-34) by 92 runs.

Rashid Khan produced a sensational six-wicket haul as Afghanistan thrashed Ireland by 92 runs in the second ODI at Bready Cricket Club on Friday, taking a 1-0 lead in the five-match series.After the opening ODI was abandoned without a toss due to rain, the second game was also delayed by inclement weather and eventually reduced to 47 overs per side. Afghanistan, led by Ibrahim Zadran, posted 299 for 8 before Rashid ripped through Ireland's batting line-up, bowling them out for 207 in 33.4 overs.Asked to bat first in overcast conditions, Afghanistan initially found it difficult against Ireland's new-ball movement. Mark Adair opened with a maiden, but Jai Moondra struggled to contain Rahmanullah Gurbaz, conceding four boundaries in his first two overs.Gurbaz briefly took Moondra apart with a six and a four in the left-arm seamer's third over, but the bowler had the last laugh when the opener attempted another big shot and holed out.Sediqullah Atal kept the scoring moving, while Ibrahim initially played a more measured innings.Afghanistan reached 65 for 1 before the pair took control, putting together a 116-run partnership.Ibrahim shifted gears and brought up his half-century from 52 balls. Atal's dismissal in the 25th over ended the stand, but Ibrahim continued to anchor the innings.The Afghanistan captain then added 43 with Rahmat Shah before both fell within two overs. Another 43-run partnership between Azmatullah Omarzai and Darwish Rasooli kept Afghanistan on course, while Hashmatullah Shahidi provided a late flourish with a 21-ball 36, including four boundaries in the final two overs.Despite losing three wickets for 21 runs late on, Afghanistan finished with a formidable 299 for 8.Ireland made a confident start in the chase, reaching 65 for 1 despite losing Paul Stirling early.Andy Balbirnie looked fluent, while Cade Carmichael, playing only his fourth ODI, launched an aggressive counterattack. Carmichael smashed Saleem Safi for 21 runs in the 14th over and went on to bring up his maiden ODI fifty from 44 balls.But Afghanistan's spinners soon changed the game.Rashid struck twice in quick succession to remove Balbirnie and Harry Tector, leaving Ireland in need of a substantial partnership. Carmichael and Lorcan Tucker attempted to rebuild, but their 38-run stand ended when Tucker was run out after losing track of the ball during an LBW appeal.Carmichael followed in the next over for 62, leaving Ireland at 152 for 5.Ben Calitz and Curtis Campher briefly threatened to revive the chase, smashing 41 runs in three overs, including five fours and two sixes. Rashid ended that assault by dismissing Calitz, triggering a stunning collapse.Ireland lost their final four wickets for just nine runs, with Rashid claiming three of them to complete remarkable figures of 6-34.The third ODI will be played on Monday, August 10, at the Civil Service Cricket Club in Belfast.
Article Summary: Afghanistan beat Ireland by 92 runs in second ODI at Bready Cricket Club. Ibrahim Zadran and Sediqullah Atal put on 116 for the first wicket. Cade Carmichael and Andy Balbirnie scored 62 and 36 respectively. Rashid Khan took six wickets for just nine runs.

Article Title: How Harsh fought through pain to script CWG history, now targets Asiad medal
Article Text:
How judoka Harsh overcame pain

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Harsh Singh's right knee still swells. It still hurts. Every time the Indian judoka steps onto the mat, he is reminded of the ACL and meniscus tear that nearly derailed his career. But at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, pain took a back seat as the 23-year-old scripted history by becoming India's first-ever men's judo gold medallist."The pain never really goes away," Singh told TOI in an interview on Thursday. "Sometimes my knee still swells up and feels tight. During the CWG, I felt the pain and the knee occasionally got swollen. After surgery, the joint never became exactly the way it was before. There's always a little discomfort during fights. You have to ignore it and continue. The medal kept me going."The historic triumph came less than a year after Singh tore his ACL and meniscus while training at the Inspire Institute of Sport (IIS) in Aug 2025. Surgery followed in Oct last in Bengaluru before a year-long rehabilitation helped him return to competition."I was in rehabilitation for almost a year. The entire coaching team at the IIS, recovery specialists and Spencer sir (Mackay, S&C expert) helped me throughout.They rebuilt my strength step by step. Because of the IIS and their entire team, I was able to come back on the mat, qualify for the CWG and represent India," he said.The comeback demanded another battle off the mat. Months away from competition saw his weight rise to nearly 72kg, forcing him to shed more than 12kg to return to his 60kg category. Gold at a ranking tournament and bronze at the senior National championships sealed his place in India's CWG squad.Despite lingering discomfort, Singh dominated in Glasgow, with only a hard-fought semifinal stretching him before he clinched the historic title."The semifinal (against the Australian Pedro Carlos) was the toughest. In the 60kg category, even a small point can decide the match. We didn't want to concede anything and stayed aggressive," he recalled.With CWG gold secured, Singh has already shifted his attention to next year's Asian Games. Training stints in Japan and South Korea are part of his preparations as he looks to bridge the gap with Asia's best."I want to improve my speed, grip and strength. Japanese and Korean players are very fast, so training there will help," he said.Born into a modest family, with his father working as a daily-wage labourer, Singh once trained without owning a judo uniform. Support from the govt's schemes and a privately funded athletes' training centre changed the course of his career."My life has changed because of this medal. More people have started noticing judo," he said. "But the best compliment came from my family. They told me, 'You have made the entire family proud.' That meant more than anything else."Having conquered injury to create CWG history, Singh's next aim is clear — turning a gritty comeback into an Asian Games podium finish.
Article Summary: Harsh Singh became India's first-ever men's judo gold medallist. The 23-year-old tore his ACL and meniscus while training at the Inspire Institute of Sport. Surgery followed in Oct last in Bengaluru before a year-long rehabilitation helped him return to competition.

Article Title: Aqib Nabi's India call-up will inspire Jammu & Kashmir cricketers: Bowling Coach Krishnakumar
Article Text:
Aquib Nabi has earned his maiden India call-up for the two-match Test series against Sri Lanka (BCCI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What matters most when selecting a player for Test cricket? Consistency over time Current form Ability to perform in tough conditions 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

While there is ongoing debate over whether India’s Test selections increasingly favour IPL performances over sustained success in domestic cricket, Jammu & Kashmir bowling coach P Krishnakumar believes Aquib Nabi’s inclusion in the national squad will reinforce players’ faith in the traditional route to top-tier selection.Nabi, who was drafted into India’s squad for the upcoming Test series in Sri Lanka after Jasprit Bumrah’s injury, earned his place on the back of consistent Ranji Trophy performances. Reacting to the call-up, Krishnakumar said the selection sends an important message to aspiring cricketers.“I would not say it’s a late inclusion of Nabi in the national side because it is about picking the best combination for the country. It took some time but ultimately it happened. I’m sure this will definitely develop belief among aspiring cricketers across the country, especially in J&K, where players train in tough conditions. If they work hard and keep performing in the domestic circuit, they will eventually get their chance to play for the country,” Krishnakumar said.“In the IPL, because you are playing against the top players, it gives you a little bit of an edge.But Nabi’s selection will create belief. The selectors have reinforced the idea that if you perform consistently in domestic cricket, you will get an opportunity to play for the country,” he added.The coach said Nabi’s transformation into an international-ready fast bowler was the result of two years of meticulous preparation. “There is a lot of hard work behind this (selection). For the last two years, Nabi has upskilled his bowling,” he said. “We had several sessions where we worked on his swing, moving the ball, bowling on different pitches with different balls and in different conditions. We trained in the morning, afternoon and evening, in both very cold and very hot weather.The preparation was thorough. He has worked extremely hard to develop himself as a fast bowler.”According to Krishnakumar, succeeding on the flat wickets common in domestic cricket demanded a significant upgrade in Nabi’s skill set. “The pitches in domestic cricket are very flat and good for batting. To take wickets, you need high-quality skills. Aquib has worked very hard on that aspect,” he said. “Over the last two years, he was trying to get into the Indian team. I told him there was no point wasting time thinking over things he couldn’t control. What he could control was his preparation.”Assessing Nabi’s strengths, Krishnakumar described him as “fantastic when it comes to moving the ball” and said his natural length is well suited to red-ball cricket. At the same time, he urged patience, stressing that international cricket presents a far greater challenge than the domestic game. “Although he has done well on the India ‘A’ tour of Lanka, there is a difference in the quality of cricket,” Krishnakumar said. “We have to give him a chance and back him. Gautam bhai (head coach gautam Gambhir) will definitely give him the freedom and space to work. If he gets that backing, he will become a better bowler.”
Article Summary: Aquib Nabi has earned his maiden India call-up for the two-match Test series against Sri Lanka. Jammu & Kashmir bowling coach P Krishnakumar believes Nabi's inclusion in the national squad will reinforce players' faith in the traditional route to top-tier selection.

Article Title: Bodoland FC register emphatic 3-0 victory; Shillong Derby ends all square
Article Text:
Bodoland FC players after their win in Guwahati (Credit: Durand Cup Media)

KOLKATA: Fortunes took a turn for both Bodoland FC and FC1 after their second match of the 135th Durand Cup on Thursday.Having been subject to a painful loss in the opener against NorthEast United FC, Bodoland came back in dominating fashion with a 3-0 win over newcomers FC1 at Indira Gandhi Athletic Stadium in Guwahati.The visitors from the north to the Assam capital, however, could not follow up on their debut win against Karbi Anglong Morning Star FC despite staying ahead of Bodoland on the Group F table in second position with three points from two games. Bodoland, on third, also had three points from their two games.Robinson Rendon (57th min) put Bodoland ahead just past the hour, heading home from skipper Holicharan Narzary’s cross after twice missing similar chances earlier. Substitutes Rituraj Mohan (78’) and Aron Thapa (81’) then turned the lead into a rout inside four second-half minutes, both scoring within a quarter of an hour of being introduced, timing that owed at least as much to head coach Vikash Panthi’s reading of the game as it did to the finishers themselves.Earlier, at the coin toss, FC1 captain Ikhlaq Fayaz presented his Bodoland counterpart, Narzary, with a sapling, a symbol of the water-conservation and climate-awareness campaign that has quietly shaped FC1’s Durand Cup debut.Shillong derby ends in thrilling 2-2 draw: Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Shillong was witness to a classic state derby as Langsning FC made a brilliant comeback to hold Nongkseh SS&CC to a 2-2 draw in a Group E Shillong derby in the evening.After Shano Tariang (29’) and Hardycliff Nongbri had put Nongkseh ahead in the space of nine minutes, Mebanshngain Kurkalang (48’) and Syed Ahmed (50’) took just two minutes of the second half to restore parity to the game.Although both teams kept gunning for a late winner, the clubs had to share honours in the end. While Langsning kept their top spot in the group with four points from two matches, Nongkseh stayed on third, behind Shillong Lajong, with just a point from their two fixtures.Today’s Matches (August 7): SC Delhi vs Defenders FC (Group C), 4:00 PM, Birsa Munda Football Stadium, Ranchi; East Bengal FC vs South United FC (Group A), 7:00 PM, Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan, Kolkata
Article Summary: Bodoland FC beat FC1 3-0 in their second match of the 135th Durand Cup. Langsning FC held Nongkseh SS&CC to a thrilling 2-2 draw in a Group E Shillong derby in the evening.

Article Title: Lakshya Sen trains in Guwahati to prepare for BWF World Championships
Article Text:
Lakshya Sen (PTI Photos)

NEW DELHI: Lakshya Sen has made a strategic switch in his preparations for the BWF World Championships here, shifting his training from the Centre for Badminton Excellence (formerly PPBA) in Bengaluru to the BAI’s National Centre of Excellence in Guwahati’s Amingaon to acclimatise to challenging stadium conditions similar to the Indira Gandhi (IG) indoor stadium – the venue for the tournament beginning Aug 17.TOI has reliably learnt that India's leading men’s singles medal hope reached the 16-court, 40,000-square-foot facility on Thursday and began preparations with light sessions and warm-up matches. He is expected to train in Guwahati for a period of five days. Sen's primary foreign coach, South Korea's Yoo Yong-sung, has accompanied the shuttler to GuwahatiThe move is aimed at ensuring the same court drift and wind conditions that troubled him earlier this year do not derail his campaign at the Worlds. Sen wants to replicate the feel of a large indoor arena, where air-conditioning, high ceilings and swirling airflow significantly influence shuttle movement, unlike an academy setting.The decision stems from his experience at the India Open in Jan this year, where he heartbreakingly bowed out in the quarters after a 17-21, 21-13, 21-18 defeat to Chinese Taipei's Lin Chun-yi. Sen later admitted he struggled to adjust to the pronounced drift inside the stadium, particularly around the net, leading to crucial unforced errors before finding his rhythm too late.The Guwahati centre, designed with a high roof and spacious layout, offers conditions closer to those expected in Delhi, allowing Sen to fine-tune his control and anticipation under similar airflow patterns.It is learnt Sen is the only Indian player to move his training specifically for this purpose. While Ayush Shetty and PV Sindhu continue training in Bengaluru and Unnati Hooda remains at her base, India’s doubles and mixed doubles players are preparing at the Pullela Gopichand Academy in Hyderabad. Elite Bulgarian women’s doubles pair Gabriela and Stefani Stoeva are also training at the Guwahati facility ahead of the Worlds.
Article Summary: Lakshya Sen has made a strategic switch in his preparations for the BWF World Championships. Sen has shifted his training from the Centre for Badminton Excellence (formerly PPBA) in Bengaluru to the BAI’s National Centre of Excellence in Guwahati. The move is aimed at ensuring the same court drift and wind conditions that troubled him earlier this year do not derail his campaign at the Worlds.

Article Title: Indian hockey mental conditioning coach Paddy Upton turns to AI to break language barrier
Article Text:
Indian team during a training session with Paddy Upton in Eindhoven on Thursday

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: For foreign experts working with Indian athletes, language is often the biggest hurdle. With not every player comfortable communicating in English, overseas coaches and support staff frequently rely on translators within the team. The arrangement, while functional, can make conversations impersonal and, in sensitive situations, cause nuances to be lost in translation.To bridge that gap, Indian men’s hockey mental conditioning coach Paddy Upton has turned to artificial intelligence. Beginning with the upcoming FIH World Cup later this month, the renowned South African mental conditioning expert will introduce an AI-powered digital twin of himself.“It’s new to the sports world,” Upton told TOI in an exclusive interaction.“I would call it a digital twin or a digital version of me. Using artificial intelligence (AI), I have taken everything I’ve written and every conversation I’ve been able to record over 25 years of mental coaching, and trained an AI mental coaching twin of myself,” he explained.Upton spent the last four months developing the WhatsApp-based programme with the help of some of India’s leading AI developers.Explaining the thinking behind the project, Upton, who has worked extensively with Indian athletes, including the men’s cricket team, said the idea stemmed from the limitations he faced while working with players who were not fluent in English.“With some players who don’t have good English skills, I wasn’t able to provide really good mental coaching support because of the language barrier. Previously, I would sit with a translator from within the team. But if it was something deeply personal, I knew it would either get lost in translation or the player would be hesitant because the translator was either a fellow player or a member of the support staff, which meant confidentiality was compromised. ”The players were introduced to the system on Wednesday.Explaining how it works, Upton said, “Now a player can have a conversation with me in Hindi. It’s like speaking on a WhatsApp call. The digital twin is trained to respond in Hindi, while I simultaneously see the English translation from wherever I am. The next day, I can sit with them and have a personal conversation as well.”While the languages are now restricted to Hindi and English, Upton added, “At this stage, it’s only in English and Hindi. This can fairly easily be expanded.”The 57-year-old stressed that the platform is designed to replicate his approach rather than function as a generic chatbot.“It’s an AI version of a personalised mental coach, but it is trained only on my information and speaks exactly as I would.”The timing, he said, was deliberate.“The idea was to have it ready for the World Cup so I could support players in a way that I haven't been able to before.”With a lot of his work with the team happening remotely, Upton believes the technology can significantly narrow the gap between him and the players.“It’s one of those things that's going to take time. The more they interact with it, the more they’ll understand it, and the richer the feedback and support it will be able to provide. It’s a very exciting development and a wonderful use of the technology now available to us,” he said.
Article Summary: Paddy Upton will introduce an AI-powered digital twin of himself at the World Cup. Upton spent the last four months developing the WhatsApp-based programme. The digital twin is trained to respond in Hindi, while Upton simultaneously sees the English translation from wherever he is.

Article Title: Former Indian cricketer Brijesh Patel calls for uniform coaching standards across cricket academies
Article Text:
Former cricketer Brijesh Patel (PTI Photo/Shailendra Bhojak)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Former India batter Brijesh Patel on Thursday called for greater standardisation across cricket coaching academies, saying the mushrooming of centres has left young cricketers and parents dealing with conflicting advice.Speaking at the launch of the book, Developing Champions in Cricket by Vedam Jaishankar, the seasoned administrator said: “Over the last two decades, we have witnessed an explosion of cricket coaching centres. While this is wonderful for the growth of the game, it has also created a new challenge, a lack of standardisation. Every academy claims to have the best method, while every coach has a different philosophy. Every parent receives different advice and television experts have yet another opinion. The result is often confusing.”Patel stressed that coaching cannot follow a one-size-fits-all approach, with every youngster requiring guidance tailored to their background and abilities. “Youngsters come from every background imaginable. Some come from cities with excellent facilities, while others travel from small towns.Their exposure, culture, skill levels and learning styles are different. A good coach first understands the child before teaching. And equally, a wise parent understands that every child's journey is unique,” he said.Patel also urged coaches and academies to focus on character-building. “Winning matches is important. Producing good human beings is even more important. Today, best practices are no longer optional,” Patel opined.Patel, who started an academy over four decades ago, underlined the need to create a safe and supportive environment for aspiring cricketers. “Parents want their children not just physically safe, but also emotionally secure. They must be protected from unhealthy influences, bullying, and unnecessary pressure. Creating that environment is the responsibility of every academy and every coach,” he added.
Article Summary: Brijesh Patel calls for greater standardisation across cricket coaching academies. Former India batter says mushrooming of centres has left young cricketers and parents dealing with conflicting advice. Patel stressed that coaching cannot follow a one-size-fits-all approach.

Article Title: Mohammedan SC removes Humayun Kabir as president after Rs 1.5 crore cheques bounce

Mohammedan SC removes Humayun Kabir as president

KOLKATA: In an extraordinary move, Mohammedan SC on Thursday removed Humayun Kabir as president of the club, just two months after the Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) founder was chosen to head the 135th-year-old institution’s administration.Ghazal Uz Zafar has been named the club’s new president with immediate effect.Soon after having been officially unveiled as the financially struggling club’s new president on June 6, Kabir promised to “solve the club’s financial problems.”However, it has been learnt that three of his cheques issued by him to the tune of Rs 1.5 crore to tackle the club’s financial requirements, eventually returned dishonoured by the bank as crisis over clearing players and staff members’ pending dues and other liabilities worsened.According to club sources, a notice was issued to Kabir seeking his explanation on unpaid funds but he didn’t respond to it.“The club called an executive committee meeting today and the decision to remove Mr Humayun Kabir was unanimous,” said a club official on Thursday.“The Executive Committee reviewed the Club’s prevailing financial position and discussed the immediate measures required to ensure financial and administrative continuity,” the club said in a statement.“The meeting also took note of the outstanding financial commitments of the Club and the urgent need to address its liabilities towards players, coaching staff, employees, statutory authorities, vendors and other creditors,” it further noted.
Article Summary: Mohammedan SC remove Humayun Kabir as president of the club. Ghazal Uz Zafar has been named the club’s new president with immediate effect. Kabir promised to “solve the club's financial problems” but three of his cheques issued by him to the tune of Rs 1.5 crore were returned dishonoured.

Article Title: ECB 'unhappy' as Ireland defy England's policy, host Afghanistan for ODI series
Article Text:
Afghanistan's Rashid Khan. (AP)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) is reportedly unhappy with Cricket Ireland for hosting Afghanistan in a five-match ODI series, even though England continue to play Afghanistan in ICC tournaments.The five-match ODI series between Ireland and Afghanistan began on Wednesday in Bready. According to a report in The Guardian, Ireland's decision to host Afghanistan could affect its future cricket ties with England.Ireland's move has put its relationship with the ECB under strain. England have refused to play bilateral cricket against Afghanistan because of the Taliban regime's restrictions on women's rights.The ECB's stance is based on concerns over what its chair, Richard Thompson, has described as the Taliban's "gender apartheid".However, England continue to face Afghanistan in ICC events, where tournament points and titles are at stake.The ECB's policy is supported by the UK government, but Cricket Ireland has taken a different approach. Ireland has built close ties with the Afghanistan Cricket Board and is hosting five ODIs this month.Under a reciprocal arrangement, Ireland will tour the United Arab Emirates in March next year to play Afghanistan in one Test, three ODIs and three T20Is.England previously played one-off Tests against Ireland at Lord's before the home Ashes series in 2019 and 2023. Next year, however, England have chosen to play Bangladesh in a warm-up Test instead.England's men's team also faced Afghanistan in the Champions Trophy in Lahore last year.While the ECB does not schedule bilateral matches against Afghanistan, it has supported Afghan women cricketers in other ways. This summer, it organised a tour of England for the Afghan Refugee Women's team and invited them to attend the T20 World Cup final at Lord's.Most members of the Afghanistan women's team fled the country after the Taliban returned to power in 2021 and banned women's sport. Many of the players later settled in Australia.Afghanistan remain the only ICC Full Member without a women's cricket programme, but the ICC has not suspended them.Australia, South Africa and New Zealand have also refused to play bilateral cricket against Afghanistan. Ireland, however, has joined the West Indies, Zimbabwe and the four Asian ICC Full Members in continuing bilateral cricket with Afghanistan.The ECB's relationship with Cricket Ireland has already been under pressure. England declined an invitation to take part in the proposed Euro Nations Cup next year, which would also feature Scotland, the Netherlands and Italy, citing a packed international schedule.England's men's team played a three-match T20I series in Ireland last September, but the ECB sent a second-string squad. No further men's matches between the two teams are currently scheduled.England's women's team, however, will host Ireland in a three-match ODI series next month.
Article Summary: England and Wales Cricket Board unhappy with Cricket Ireland for hosting Afghanistan in a five-match ODI series. England have refused to play bilateral cricket against Afghanistan because of the Taliban regime's restrictions on women's rights. ECB's stance is based on concerns over what its chair, Richard Thompson, has described as the Taliban's "gender apartheid" England continue to face Afghanistan in ICC events where tournament points and titles are at stake.

Article Title: After Pakistan boxer, Uganda athletes go ‘missing’ in Glasgow after CWG campaign; police intitate probe
Article Text:
Pakistani boxer Qudratullah

NEW DELHI: Scottish police are investigating reports that several athletes from Pakistan and Uganda did not return home after the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow ended last Sunday.“Police Scotland has ⁠received reports of several athletes who are unaccounted for,” a spokesperson said late on Tuesday, as quoted by Al Jazeera.“Enquiries are ongoing to assess the circumstances, and early engagement is taking ‌place with the Home Office.”Uganda’s NBS Sport reported that four of its six boxers were missing before the team was due to fly home on Tuesday. One of the athletes reportedly told the broadcaster that they planned to seek asylum. Pakistan Today also reported that one Pakistani boxer did not turn up for the return flight.Pakistani boxer Qudratullah has reportedly gone missing in Glasgow just hours before the country’s team was scheduled to leave for home. According to Geo News, Pakistan Boxing Federation sources said Qudratullah was last seen in his hotel room at around 2am.Officials later checked his room but could not find him. The Pakistani team was expected to gather in the hotel lobby at 9am before heading to the airport.His passport and return ticket are reportedly still with the team manager.Cases of athletes going missing after the Commonwealth Games have been reported in previous editions. After the 2018 Gold Coast Games, authorities were still searching for 50 athletes and officials a month later, while another 190 had sought asylum.Pakistan’s 21-member contingent ended the 2026 Commonwealth Games with just one medal. Boxer Fatima Zahra won bronze in the women’s 60kg category, becoming the first Pakistani female boxer to win a Commonwealth Games medal.The result was Pakistan’s lowest medal tally since 1998. Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem also missed out on a medal despite being one of the country’s biggest hopes.
Article Summary: Pakistani boxer Qudratullah has reportedly gone missing in Glasgow. He was last seen in his hotel room at around 2am. The Pakistani team was expected to gather in the hotel lobby at 9am before heading to the airport. Pakistani boxer Fatima Zahra won bronze in the women’s 60kg category.

Article Title: WI vs PAK 2nd Test: Babar Azam's wait for Test century continues; Pakistan on brink of victory vs West Indies
Article Text:
Pakistan captain Babar Azam once again missed out on a Test century.

Shafique's 160 helps Pakistan take first-innings lead

Babar Azam

's wait for Test hundred continues

King injured after match-changing run-out

Warrican leads West Indies bowling attack

Pakistan strikes back with the ball

NEW DELHI: Pakistan moved closer to a rare away Test win after reducing West Indies to 103/6 at stumps on Day 3 of the second and final Test. Despite West Indies holding a lead of 60 runs, the hosts have only four wickets left, giving Pakistan the upper hand heading into the fourth day.West Indies ended the day on 103/6, leading by 60 runs with only four wickets remaining.Pakistan will look to dismiss the remaining batters quickly on Day 4 and chase a modest target to secure their first away Test victory since 2023. West Indies, meanwhile, are aiming to complete a 2-0 series sweep after winning the opening Test by 90 runs.Pakistan began the day still behind West Indies' first-innings total of 344, but Abdullah Shafique produced a superb unbeaten 160 to guide his team to 387.His innings helped Pakistan secure a 43-run first-innings lead before the visitors were bowled out.Left-arm spinner Jomel Warrican starred for West Indies with six wickets for 112 runs. He cleaned up the Pakistan lower order after already removing key batters earlier in the innings.Pakistan captain Babar Azam once again missed out on a Test century.He was run out for 88 after a brilliant direct hit from Brandon King ended his 183-run partnership with Shafique.Pakistan were still trailing by 63 runs when the wicket fell.Babar attempted a quick single after pushing the ball into the off side, but Shafique changed his mind and sent him back. King collected the ball and hit the stumps with a flat throw, leaving Babar short of his ground despite a desperate dive.It was Babar's highest Test score in 35 innings, but he is still waiting for his first Test century since scoring one against New Zealand in Karachi in December 2022.Brandon King's brilliant fielding effort came at a cost.The West Indies batter injured his lower back after landing awkwardly while throwing down the stumps. He had to be taken off the field, and it remains unclear whether he will be able to bat on Day 4.Warrican was the pick of the bowlers for West Indies.He dismissed debutant Awais Zafar for 1 before Shamar Joseph trapped Salman Ali Agha lbw. Warrican then bowled Mohammad Rizwan for 18 with the second new ball and later finished the innings by taking three wickets in four deliveries to complete a six-wicket haul.West Indies made a solid start to their second innings as Tagenarine Chanderpaul and Kavem Hodge added 40 runs for the opening wicket.However, Pakistan's spinners quickly took control.Sajid Khan removed Chanderpaul and Amir Jangoo before West Indies recovered through a partnership between Shai Hope and captain Roston Chase.The visitors then lost three wickets in the final five overs of the day. Sajid trapped Hope lbw for 15 and dismissed Jayden Seales for a two-ball duck. On the last ball of the day, Chase lost his concentration and chipped a simple return catch to Ali Usman after scoring 17.Sajid finished the day with figures of 4/32, while Usman picked up 2/29.
Article Summary: West Indies end the day on 103/6, leading by 60 runs with only four wickets remaining. Abdullah Shafique produced a superb unbeaten 160 to guide his team to 387. Pakistan will look to dismiss the remaining batters quickly on Day 4 and chase a modest target.

Article Title: 'Having skill is one thing': Shikhar Dhawan drops big verdict on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi

Former India opener Shikhar Dhawan has praised teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, saying the youngster's fearless batting and ability to perform at such a young age make him special.Speaking to news agency ANI, Dhawan said it is a big achievement for a 15-year-old to reach the international level and deliver consistent performances. He also pointed to Sooryavanshi's IPL displays, saying the teenager's confidence in hitting boundaries stands out.Dhawan said talent alone is not enough, and added that having the courage and mindset to play attacking cricket at such a young age is what sets Sooryavanshi apart. And it's a very big thing that at the age of 15 or 16, reaching the international level first is a big thing in itself. Even when he was playing in the IPL. And I'm sure that his present is also very good and his future will also be very good," Dhawan said.Sooryavanshi, 15, recently enjoyed a successful T20I series against Zimbabwe, scoring 151 runs in three matches to win his maiden Player of the Series award as India completed a 3-0 clean sweep.Earlier, during the T20I series against England, Sooryavanshi became the youngest player to make his international debut for India.His India debut came after a successful IPL 2026 season with Rajasthan Royals. Article Title: 'I got angry': Ashwin reveals why he stopped talking to Sanjay Manjrekar
Article Text:
R Ashwin and Sanjay Manjrekar (Agency Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin has revealed that sharp criticism from Sanjay Manjrekar early in his career left him deeply hurt, but eventually became one of the biggest turning points in his journey as an international cricketer. Ashwin admitted that he was upset after Manjrekar questioned his fitness following his first tour of Australia, suggesting that it was affecting both his bowling and fielding. The remarks angered him at the time and even led him to distance himself from the former India batter for several years.However, instead of dwelling on the criticism, Ashwin used it as motivation to transform his game.Speaking on JioHotstar's 'Cheeky Singles', the veteran off-spinner recalled how the episode changed his outlook."I had messaged Sanjay Manjrekar once. After my first Australia tour, he had written a long article, and I read it completely while returning. After reading I got angry, getting angry is one thing, but I felt very bad. I let it go. I used to not talk a lot to him either. The next four years, I worked a lot, as I was not a gifted athlete. Then in 2015, he wrote another article saying he was bowling very well. Then I asked for his number and messaged him that your article back then changed my life.I always look at whether there is something to learn from criticism," Ashwin said.Ashwin explained that Manjrekar's criticism prompted him to work relentlessly on his fitness and overall game, eventually helping him become one of the world's leading spinners. Their relationship also improved after Manjrekar acknowledged the changes in his performances in a later article in 2015.Ashwin retired from international cricket as one of India's most decorated cricketers. Across 287 international matches, he claimed 765 wickets, including 537 in Tests, 156 in ODIs and 72 in T20Is. He finished as India's second-highest wicket-taker in international cricket, behind only Anil Kumble .Widely regarded as one of India's greatest all-rounders, Ashwin also made significant contributions with the bat, scoring six Test centuries while playing a key role in India's success in the longest format for more than a decade.Although he has retired from international and IPL cricket, Ashwin continues to feature in franchise T20 leagues around the world. He signed for the Big Bash League last season but missed the tournament due to injury before returning to action in Major League Cricket.
Article Summary: Former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin has revealed that sharp criticism from Sanjay Manjrekar early in his career left him deeply hurt. Ashwin admitted that he was upset after Manj rekar questioned his fitness following his first tour of Australia. The remarks angered him at the time and even led him to distance himself from the former India batter for several years.

Article Title: Currently fifth, what a Sri Lanka series win could mean for India's WTC campaign
Article Text:
Shubman Gill, Gautam Gambhir

What happens if India win the Sri Lanka series?

India will begin their two-match Test series against Sri Lanka on Saturday, August 15, in Galle, with valuable World Test Championship (WTC) points at stake. With less than a year left before the WTC final, Shubman Gill 's team needs a series win to strengthen its chances of qualifying.India are currently fifth in the WTC standings with a points percentage of 48.15, while Sri Lanka are sixth with 41.67. Both teams are still within reach of fourth-placed Bangladesh, who have a points percentage of 58.33.However, Bangladesh face a difficult schedule ahead. They will host the West Indies before travelling to Australia for a challenging Test series.India can win the series either 1-0 or 2-0.If India win one Test and draw the other, they will collect 16 points from the series. That will take their total to 68 points and improve their points percentage to 51.51.Sri Lanka's points percentage, in that case, will drop to 33.33.If India complete a 2-0 clean sweep, they will earn the maximum 24 points. Their total will rise to 76 points after 11 Tests, and their points percentage will improve to 57.58.For Sri Lanka, a home whitewash would reduce their points percentage to 27.78. They would remain just ahead of seventh-placed England.England currently have four wins from 13 Tests and a points percentage of 24.36.A series win will help India strengthen their hold on fifth place. They could also move above Bangladesh into fourth if Bangladesh lose their upcoming series against Australia.Even with a 2-0 win over Sri Lanka, India cannot move into the top three, with New Zealand currently third on 72.22 points percentage.
Article Summary: India will begin their two-match Test series against Sri Lanka on August 15. World Test Championship points are at stake in the series. India are currently fifth in the standings with a points percentage of 48.15. Sri Lanka are sixth with 41.67.

Article Title: No tickets required: Sri Lanka announces free stadium entry for fans in India Test series

Photo/BCCI

India vs Sri Lanka

schedule:

Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) board on Friday announced that free entry will be provided to fans for the upcoming two-match Test series against India in Galle and Colombo. The series between the subcontinental rivals forms a key part of the ongoing ICC World Test Championship 2025–2027 cycle.The two-match series begins on August 15 in Galle. The first Test will be played at the Galle International Stadium, while the second match is scheduled at the SSC in Colombo from August 23 to 27."Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) wishes to announce that public admission to the upcoming Test Series between Sri Lanka and India will be free of charge thus providing cricket fans with an excellent opportunity to witness world-class Test cricket," SLC said in a release."Sri Lanka Cricket warmly invites cricket enthusiasts, young aspiring cricketers, families, and sports fans from across the country to take advantage of this initiative and experience the excitement of international Test cricket between Sri Lanka and India," it added.Test cricket has struggled to attract crowds in Sri Lanka over the years, and even Indian teams in the past have often played in front of empty stands.Across the subcontinent, Test cricket has generally not drawn large crowds, except in a few big Test centres such as Kolkata, Chennai, Mumbai and Bengaluru.India head into the series placed fifth in the World Test Championship standings, while Sri Lanka are sixth. India last played a Test in June, when they faced Afghanistan in a one-off match in New Chandigarh. A strong performance in Sri Lanka will improve their chances of reaching the World Test Championship final.The tour will also mark the start of Subhadeep Ghosh's tenure as India's fielding coach after the BCCI decided not to extend the contracts of T Dilip and assistant coach Ryan ten Doeschate.India dominated their previous Test tour of Sri Lanka in 2017, winning the three-match series 3-0. They won the opening Test in Galle by 304 runs, followed it with an innings and 53-run victory in Colombo, and completed the clean sweep with an innings and 171-run win in Pallekele.Sri Lanka, meanwhile, enter the series after losing their recent two-Test series against the West Indies 1-0. Article Title: Jai Moondra: The Tonk boy who chased a degree and found international cricket in Ireland

Ireland's Jai Moondra before match one of the Spinny Cup Men's T20 International series between Ireland and India at Stormont in Belfast. (Photo/Getty Images)
